Park and Recreation Commission

  Inglewood, California
  August 4, 2022

A meeting of the Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission was convened on August 4,
2022, via Zoom. Commissioner Denmon called the meeting to order at 6:01 p.m. followed
by the flag salute.

Stephanie Maldonado announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Commissioner Lee Denmon - District 1, Commissioner Jacob
  Fragoso - District 2, Commissioner Cynthia McLemore - District 3,
  Commissioner Henry Brown - Commissioner at Large
  Absent:  Commissioner Christopher Beck - District Four

City Personnel present for the meeting were as follows:

  Sabrina Barnes  Parks, Recreation, and Community Services Director
  Teresa Estrada  Recreation Superintendent
  Bharat Devlia  Food Services Manager
  Gilbert Gonzalez  Graffiti Abatement Supervisor
  Stephanie Maldonado  Senior Management Assistant

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None.

MINUTES. It was moved by Commissioner Fragoso and seconded by Commissioner
McLemore that the minutes for the meeting held on July 7, 2022, be approved. The
motion was carried by the following roll call vote:

Ayes: Commissioners Fragoso, McLemore, Brown, and Denmon
Noes: None.

STAFF REPORTS.

AWARD NORTH PARK PLAYGROUND CANOPY PROJECT: CB 22-12. Staff report dated
August 4, 2022, was presented recommending the Park and Recreation Commission
recommend the Mayor and Council Members take the following actions: A. award
contract and approve agreement with R.E. Schultz Construction, Inc. in the amount of
$96,465 for the North Park Playground Canopy Project (CB-22-12); and B. approve a
contingency amount of $10,000 for a total cost of $106,465. (General Fund)

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission

It was moved by Commissioner Brown and seconded by Commissioner Fragoso that the
Commission hereby approves the staff report. The motion was carried by the following
roll call vote:

Ayes: Commissioners Fragoso, Brown, McLemore, and Denmon
Noes: None.

EDWARD VINCENT PARK IMPROVEMENT PROJECT - PUMP TRACK. Staff report dated
August 4, 2022, was presented recommending the Park and Recreation Commission
recommend the Mayor and Council Members approve Amendment No. 1 of Agreement
No. 21-082 between the City of Inglewood and Grow Cycling Foundation for the
installation of a Pump Track at Edward Vincent Jr. Park. (General Fund)

It was moved by Commissioner McLemore and seconded by Commissioner Fragoso that
the Commission hereby approves the staff report. The motion was carried by the
following roll call vote:

Ayes: Commissioners Fragoso, McLemore, Brown, and Denmon
Noes: None.

DIRECTOR’S BUSINESS.

REPORTS - PARKS ADMINISTRATION The Graffiti Abatement Supervisor, Gilbert Gonzalez
reported that the Parks Division replaced two springs that were damaged on the teeter
totters at North and Vincent Parks playgrounds. The Division spread 16 yards of a wood
fiber in the playground area at North Park, repaired a broken mainline (irrigation) at
Rogers Park, and replaced seven rubber tiles at Center Park’s playground. Graffiti
Abatement has been quite busy in both Districts 2 and 3 around the intersections of
Eucalyptus and Florence Avenues. They have also been busy with the restrooms at Rogers
Park. The new Metro Rail walls and bridge running westbound on Florence Avenue
towards La Cienega Boulevard are being heavily tagged. We do receive numerous calls for
graffiti in that area however Metro is responsible for the graffiti on their property. To
report graffiti in the Metro Rail area, please call (213) 922-5931 or you can send pictures
via email to mehelpdesk@metro.net.

REPORTS - RECREATION. The Recreation Superintendent, Teresa Estrada reported.
Summer time is the peak season for the Department. Over 800 kids participated in our
Summer Day Camp Program, reaching full capacity at all three camp locations Rogers,
Darby, and Siminski Parks. Summer Camps culminate on August 12, 2022. We added a
few new programs and activities to camp this summer including enrichment programs,
and STEM, the enrichment component was a plus, with tons of positive feedback from

  2
   Park and Recreation Commission

the parents along with a request to continue it next year. 400 participants took part in
our swim offerings, we offer youth and adult swim lessons, and parent and me swim
lessons for youth 6 months to 6 years of age. We added lap swim this year. General swim
daily consisted of 100 to 200 participants. Movies in the Park is the first event Parks and
Recreation held since the pandemic. The event was attended by over 300 people. Another
Movies in the Park series will be held at North Park in conjunction with Councilman
Padilla's Chili Cook-off and Annual Picnic on August 13, 2022. Dodgers Dreamteam
consisted of two Spring Leagues for the younger youth and a Summer League for the
older. 500 youth were served within both leagues. Currently, we have 279 players in our
Summer League which culminates on August 20, 2022, with the final games being held at
Darby Park. Night at the Bowl featuring Ricky Martin was held July 22, 2022, at Hollywood
Bowl. Transportation was provided to and from Inglewood City Hall. A second concert is
scheduled for August 26, 2022, and will feature Diana Ross.

REPORTS - HUMAN SERVICES. The Food Services Manager, Bharat Devlia reported the
Nutrition Program serves approximately 350 seniors per week and continues to provide
LA Food Bank boxes monthly and fresh produce weekly. Our Nutrition staff including our
Home Delivery Meals staff continue to be dedicated to serving and delivering our seniors
their daily meals. Our dining room is closed for congregate dining due to COVID and there
is no projected opening date yet. Our Summer Food Program started on June 13, 2022.
We are serving at seven different locations to youth 18 and under. The sites are Ashwood
Park, Crenshaw Library, Darby Park, Siminiski Park, Lockhaven Community Center, Rogers
Park, and Edward Vincent, Jr. Park. We are providing breakfast, lunch, and snacks at
different sites and the times will vary according to the sites. The Child and Adult Care Food
Program (CACFP) was successful and our audit was completed with no findings. The
pogrom provided Grab-N-Go meals to youth 18 and younger at three sites (Crenshaw
Library, Rogers Park, and Darby Park). Our Senior and Disabled Paratransit service
continues to provide trips to critical appointments such as dialysis and doctors'
appointments. Drivers as well as passengers continue to wear facemasks coverings. We
have also been scheduling seniors and persons with disabilities to other next-day
requested appointments, and if resources are available, same-day service requests may
be serviced as well. Seniors are still expected to wear face coverings, have their
temperatures checked, practice safe distancing and provide proof of full vaccination.
These measures are required to enter and participate in activities. These measures will
continue until further notice as we continue to ensure our seniors are as safe as possible.

REPORTS - DIRECTOR. The Director of Parks, Recreation, and Community Services,
Sabrina Barnes reported she and staff are excited to be "open", serving our kids, and
adults and seeing how well received our activities and programs have been. She
commended the staff for the work they do.

  3
   Park and Recreation Commission

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None.

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS. Commissioner Brown complimented the staff on a job well
done.

There being no further business to be presented, Commissioner Denmon declared the
meeting adjourned at 6:26 p.m.
